name: Question 4
problem:
Consider the type I region $R,$ given by

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,(x,y)\in D,\,-1\le z\le \sqrt{3{x}^{2}+2{y}^{2}}},
$$

where $D$ is some finite region in the $xy$-plane. Then,

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V=
$$
worked_solution:
A type I region in three-dimensional space can be written as

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,(x,y)\in D,\,{u}_{1}(x,y)\le z\le {u}_{2}(x,y)}.
$$

A typical three-dimensional type I region can be visualized schematically, as shown below.

![](@asset-0@)

 

If $R$ is a type I region, we can express the triple integral of $f(x,y,z)$ over $R$ as a mixed integral, as follows:

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={∬}_{D}[{\int }_{{u}_{1}(x,y)}^{{u}_{2}(x,y)}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}z]\,\text{d}A
$$

In our case, we have

$$
{u}_{1}(x,y)=-1\,{u}_{2}(x,y)=\sqrt{3{x}^{2}+2{y}^{2}}.
$$

Therefore, our triple integral can be written as

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={∬}_{D}[{\int }_{-1}^{\sqrt{3{x}^{2}+2{y}^{2}}}f(x,y,z)\,dz]dA.
$$

Question 4

Consider the type I region R, given by R={(x,y,z):(x,y)∈D,−1≤z≤3x2+2y2}, where D is some finite region in the xy-plane. Then, ∭Rf(x,y,z)dV=

a
∫−13x2+2y2[∬Df(x,y,z)dA]dz
b
∬D[∫−13x2+2y2f(x,y,z)dz]dA
c
∬D[∫−13x2+2y2f(x,y,z)dA]dy
d
∬D[∫−13x2+2y2f(x,y,z)dx]dA
e
∬D[∫−13x2+2y2f(x,y,z)dy]dA
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

A type I region in three-dimensional space can be written as R={(x,y,z):(x,y)∈D,u1(x,y)≤z≤u2(x,y)}.

A typical three-dimensional type I region can be visualized schematically, as shown below.

If R is a type I region, we can express the triple integral of f(x,y,z) over R as a mixed integral, as follows: ∭Rf(x,y,z)dV=∬D[∫u1(x,y)u2(x,y)f(x,y,z)dz]dA

In our case, we have u1(x,y)=−1u2(x,y)=3x2+2y2.

Therefore, our triple integral can be written as ∭Rf(x,y,z)dV=∬D[∫−13x2+2y2f(x,y,z)dz]dA.
